HARD NEGATIVE: man lying beside a railway track, two soldiers crouched over him, one bystander standing. The crouches must not outrank the fall in the top-1 reduction - inference.js ranks any `fall` first, and this is what pins that. From the 2023 corpus (Roboflow fallsdata2, CC BY 4.0), 640x640 as exported. expectedAll added 2026-08-12: one soldier reads `squat` at tier A (knee 78deg, hips 0.81 over ankles) and this is the ONLY assertion of a correct squat anywhere in the harness - top-1 cannot express it, because the fall correctly outranks it. Not a substitute for a clean single-subject squat fixture, which the class still lacks

HARD NEGATIVE: woman down on a street, police officer squatting beside her, bystanders bending and standing. Same property as the rail fixture on a different scene - a crouching bystander is the single most common false-fall shape in this domain, and posture.js's AMBIGUOUS_TORSO_ANGLE band had no fixture at all before these two. CC BY 4.0. expectedAll added 2026-08-12: the officer is the harness's second asserted squat (knee 58deg, hips 0.56 over ankles). Two of the five reads are tier D - bystanders with no visible torso - and are pinned deliberately: they are what a change to NMS or the person floor would disturb first

Badminton player flat on her back, shot from directly overhead, knees drawn up. Her torso runs vertically in the image so torsoAngle reads 10deg - upright - and every leg feature said `sit` until the kneeling gate (thighShinRatio >= 2.5) was added. This is the fixture that proves that gate earns its keep. CC BY 4.0

KNOWN GAP - EXPECTED TO FAIL. Man face-down on a floor, lying along the camera's view axis. torsoAngle 2.5deg, kneeDrop 1.14, kneeAngle 168deg, thighShinRatio 1.29: every feature reads as a standing person, and the aspect>=1.5 escape hatch misses because the box is narrow (0.45). MODEL_CARD predicted exactly this - 'a fall that is both foreshortened and narrow-boxed will still be missed'. Kept as a failing fixture on purpose: it is the boundary of what 2D keypoint geometry can express, and it should stay visible in the accuracy number rather than be quietly excluded. CC BY 4.0

KNOWN GAP - EXPECTED TO FAIL. Person on the ground beside a bus with three people crouched over them. The pose model never detects the fallen subject at all - it finds the three crouchers and two bystanders and nothing else - so this is a *detection* miss, not a posture miss, and no change to posture.js can fix it. Distinguishing it from prone-fall-view-axis is the point of keeping both. CC BY 4.0

Man flat on his back on a dojo mat. This is the frame that found both 2026-08-12 fall gates: it returned `sit` at 0.77 before them. torsoAngle 25.4deg is under the 50 gate, and the wide-box hatch used to also demand torsoAngle >= 30, so it missed by 4.6deg; kneeDrop -1.11 then made the sit branch claim him. Now caught by `aspect >= 1.5` alone (box 1.96) at 0.77, and would also be caught by the inverted gate. The ONLY real-image coverage for either gate - everything else pinning them is a synthetic skeleton in posture-check.mjs. Survives 6/6. Source: youtube.com/watch?v=ctniCxIdpTY, an aikido demo the repo owner states is free to reuse and screen-recorded himself; licence not independently verified from the YouTube licence field

Two men standing on a dojo mat, both full-body, camera near floor height. Added for camera-height diversity - MODEL_CARD identifies elevation as the largest systematic source of missed falls, and before this every stand fixture was eye-level. expectedAll pins both, so a regression that drops or misreads the second subject cannot hide behind top-1. Survives 6/6. Same source and licence caveat as dojo-fall-wide-box.jpg

FIRST TRUE POSITIVE FOR `squat`. Deep bodyweight squat, front-on, full body with both ankles visible - the squat gate is tier-A only, so a fixture without ankles would test the sit fallback instead. knee 58deg, hips 0.95 over ankles, conf 0.56. Before these the class appeared in the confusion matrix only as a false positive and was excluded from macro-F1 entirely. Survives 5/6 (fails downscale-320). Supplied by the repo owner as one panel of an 8-panel gym contact sheet, cropped to 304x336; provenance not independently verified

Same squat from behind, and the deepest of the set - knee 16.6deg, thigh only 0.17x its own shin. That thigh ratio is far under SIT_THIGH_FORESHORTEN (0.75), so this fixture is what pins the *gate ordering*: the squat gate runs before the thigh gate precisely so a deep crouch is not claimed as a sit first, and MODEL_CARD records that reversing them costs 24 crouches. Reverse the order and this fixture goes red. Survives 6/6

Same squat in profile. knee 67deg, hips 0.79 over ankles, conf 0.47 - the lowest-confidence pass in the set, so it is also the closest thing the harness has to a squat confidence floor. Survives 6/6. Side-on matters because the front and back views foreshorten the thigh while this one does not, so the three together exercise the gate with the thigh in and out of the image plane

KNOWN GAP - EXPECTED TO FAIL. Same squat, three-quarter view, returns `sit` at 0.76. A genuine deep squat that misses the squat gate on its UPPER bound: hipAnkleDrop is 1.05 against a SQUAT_HIP_ANKLE_DROP ceiling of 1.0, so it falls through to the thigh gate (0.51x shin) and reads sit. Measured 2026-08-12, the ceiling should NOT be raised to fix this: moving 1.0 -> 1.05 newly claims 27 corpus detections of which only 3 are real squats and 7 are falls, and a fall relabelled `squat` is a missed alarm. Kept failing to make that trade visible - the next person to see a squat read as `sit` will want to move that number, and this fixture is the argument against it. Note it is a knife-edge, not a clean miss: it fails clean, grayscale, dark-40% and downscale-320, but PASSES hflip, blur-3px and crop-80%, because those nudge the keypoints just far enough to put hipAnkleDrop back under 1.0. A fixture that flips on a 0.05 margin is the honest picture of a threshold boundary
